findings.title: is_sha256 accepts a single trailing newline via $ regex anchor
findings.body: primitives.py _SHA256_RE = re.compile(r'^[a-f0-9]{64}$') combined with .match() admits a trailing newline (Python $ matches before a trailing newline). Weakens the exact-digest binding invariant that DigestRef and Receipt rely on. Untested in either direction.

findings.title: test_valid_floats_accepted has a tautological assertion
findings.body: tests/unit/uag/test_hardening.py::TestCanonicalJsonRejectsNonStandardFloats::test_valid_floats_accepted asserts ("0.0" not in result or "0" in result), which is satisfied regardless of actual float-serialization behavior and does not meaningfully verify the intended -0.0 handling.

remaining_risks: Independent audit ran tools/MCP-disabled (static analysis only); no in-audit test execution or live git/gh cross-check. Deterministic suites (72 unit / 187 contracts / ruff / diff-check / change-contract) were run by the implementer, not the auditor.
Enum-value fidelity to ratified C0-R2 common_defs.schema.json could not be byte-verified (schema file not present in this checkout); only internal self-consistency was checked.
is_sha256 trailing-newline gap (AUD-01) is unpatched and untested as of this head.
